skill.name: rdkit
skill.description: Use RDKit for cheminformatics workflows that need molecule parsing, descriptor calculation, fingerprints, substructure search, reactions, coordinate generation, and visualization.
skill.summary: Guides precise RDKit molecule analysis, screening, and visualization workflows.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives from chemistry notation, Markdown code fences, benign RDKit examples, and user-directed output files. No prompt injection or covert external command behavior was found, but the documentation includes unsafe pickle loading guidance that can become code execution with untrusted files.

remediation.suggestion: Add a warning to load pickle files only from trusted sources, or replace the example with safer SDF, SMILES, or structured table storage.

remediation.issue: Local output examples can overwrite files
remediation.suggestion: Document that output paths should be chosen carefully, and consider examples that check before overwriting existing files.

semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md recommends loading molecules with pickle.load without warning users to trust the file. Loading an attacker-controlled pickle can execute Python code.

content.value_statement: Cheminformatics work often needs precise molecule parsing, descriptor calculation, and structure search. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through RDKit workflows with focused references and scripts.
actual_capabilities: Guides SMILES, SDF, MOL, and InChI molecule parsing and writing.
Explains descriptor calculation for molecular weight, LogP, TPSA, and Lipinski checks.
Documents fingerprint workflows with Tanimoto, Dice, and Cosine similarity metrics.
Provides SMARTS pattern references for functional groups and substructure filters.
Includes scripts for molecular properties, similarity search, and substructure filtering.
Covers reactions, 2D and 3D coordinates, and molecular visualization.
limitations: Requires RDKit in the local Python environment.
Does not install dependencies or manage conda environments.
Example scripts read and write local files chosen by the user.
Pickle examples should only be used with trusted files.

use_cases.title: Screen Compound Libraries
use_cases.description: Filter molecule files by descriptors, SMARTS patterns, and similarity thresholds.

use_cases.title: Prepare Molecular Features
use_cases.description: Generate RDKit descriptors and fingerprints for QSAR, clustering, or model input.

use_cases.title: Build Chemistry Workflows
use_cases.description: Adapt RDKit examples into local scripts for parsing, visualization, and batch processing.

prompt_templates.title: Calculate Basic Properties
prompt_templates.prompt: Use RDKit to analyze this SMILES string: CCO. Report molecular weight, LogP, TPSA, donors, and acceptors.

prompt_templates.title: Filter a Compound File
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an RDKit plan to filter molecules.smi for benzene rings and exclude acyl chlorides. Include expected output files.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Similar Molecules
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Morgan fingerprints to compare a query SMILES against database.sdf. Explain threshold choice and result ranking.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Screening Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an RDKit workflow for library triage using descriptors, PAINS filters, similarity clustering, and molecule images.

output_examples.output: A concise property summary with molecular weight, LogP, TPSA, donors, acceptors, rotatable bonds, and Lipinski status.

output_examples.input: Find benzene-containing molecules in a SMILES file.
output_examples.output: A filtering plan that names the SMARTS pattern, expected pass counts, output file, and match report.

output_examples.input: Compare a query molecule to a small SDF library.
output_examples.output: A ranked hit list with similarity scores, fingerprint method, threshold, and notes about borderline matches.

best_practices: Validate every parsed molecule before calculating descriptors or fingerprints.
Use streaming suppliers for large SDF files to control memory use.
Record fingerprint type, radius, bit length, and similarity metric with results.
anti_patterns: Do not use descriptor outputs as experimental proof without expert review.
Do not load pickled molecule files from untrusted sources.
Do not share mutable MolSupplier objects across worker threads.

faq.question: What is this skill best for?
faq.answer: It is best for precise RDKit guidance in cheminformatics and molecular data workflows.

faq.question: Does it install RDKit?
faq.answer: No. RDKit must already be available in the local Python environment.

faq.question: Can it process SDF and SMILES files?
faq.answer: Yes. The references and scripts cover SDF, MOL, SMILES, and related molecule inputs.

faq.question: Can it generate molecule images?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation covers RDKit drawing APIs for single molecules and molecule grids.

faq.question: Is it suitable for drug discovery workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports common screening tasks, but results still need scientific validation.

faq.question: Does it send molecule data to external services?
faq.answer: No evidence found. The reviewed examples use local RDKit APIs and local files.
